Good news for Tamil cinema fans and producers. On November 3, the Tamil Nadu government announced that theatres across the state can screen newly released Tamil films up to six times a day for the first week after release, with shows running from 6 AM to 2:30 AM the next day.

dff5de13b0.title: Sandeep Reddy Vanga hits back at those blaming cinema after the Anantapur school attack
dff5de13b0.headline: Sandeep Reddy Vanga hits back at those blaming cinema after the Anantapur school attack
dff5de13b0.caption:
Filmmaker Sandeep Reddy Vanga has responded on X after a section of social media linked his film Animal to the recent attack on a student at a school in Anantapur district, Andhra Pradesh. He said the first response to such a crime should be empathy and an effort to understand the larger problem, not finding "a convenient scapegoat in cinema."

He also hit out at some actors, directors and producers in the industry, accusing them of using the tragedy to take a dig at his work. Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma has also said blaming films for rising violence is misplaced.

Do films influence real-life behaviour, or is cinema being made a scapegoat? Share your views respectfully in the comments.

5e87819159.title: Malayalam cinema bids farewell to Pulimurugan cinematographer Shaji Kumar, who passed away at 57
5e87819159.headline: Malayalam cinema bids farewell to Pulimurugan cinematographer Shaji Kumar, who passed away at 57
5e87819159.caption:
Renowned cinematographer Shaji Kumar passed away in the early hours of November 10 at a private hospital in Kochi. He was 57. He was taken ill on November 7 while shooting a Dileep film in Alappuzha and was moved to Kochi, where he died of cardiac failure.

Shaji Kumar began his career as an independent cinematographer with Uthaman in 2001 and went on to shoot some of Malayalam cinema's biggest films, including Pulimurugan, Naran, Odiyan, Pokkiri Raja, Ramaleela, Pathonpatham Noottandu and Thudarum. In Tamil, he worked on Ponnar Shankar, Mambattiyan and Saahasam. His last works include Mohanlal's Athimanoharam, directed by Tharun Moorthy.

Rest in peace, Shaji Kumar. Thank you for the visuals that made us fall in love with cinema.
